full_judgment:
judgment and order dated 21.7.2008 of the High Court Division passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3417 of 2008, arising out of Session Case No.841 of 2007 corresponding to C.R. Case No. 183 of 2007, under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, the Act, discharging the Rule. Facts, in brief, are that the respondent No. I filed the above C.R. Case alleging that on 27.8.2006 and 26.10.2006 the petitioner, from his own account lying with Hong Kong and Sanghi Banking Corporation Limited, (HSBC), issued two cheques for Tk.62,41,118/- and Tk.30,00,000/-respectively in his favour and subsequently those cheques were dishonored on 28.8.2006 and 20.10.2006 respectively due to insufficient fund and then on 14.32007 the respondent No. 1 served a legal notice upon the petitioner demanding payment and the petitioner received the said notice on 203.2007 but did not make any payment. Eventually the learned Metropolitan Additional Session Judge, by order dated 23.9.2007, framed charge against the petitioner under section 138 of the Act and meanwhile the examination of the witnesses has been completed. The petitioner then filed an application before the High Court Division under section 561A Cr.P.C and obtained Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.34I7 of 2008 and the learned Advocate of the respondents opposed the Rule contending that the petition of complaint of the C.R. Case No. 183 of 2007 clearly discloses cause of action as the petitioner duly received the notice for payment and further the trial has been concluded and the case is fixed for argument. The High Court Division, after hearing, discharged the Rule. 

 3. As it appears the High Court Division discharged the Rule holding that the petitioner issued cheques on 27.8.2006 and 26.10.2006 and those were lastly dishonored on 18.2.2007 and 22.2.2007 respectively and thereafter on 18.3.2007 the respondent No.1 served legal notice upon the petitioner demanding payment and the petitioner received the said notice on 203.2007 and thereafter on 83.2007 the respondent No.1 filed the above C.R. case and further all the legal formalities as laid down in section 138 of the Act were compiled and the main ground of the petitioner for praying for quashing is that he having not received the legal notice, no cause of action arose to file the case and so no offence under section 138 of the Act has also been disclosed but whether the petitioner received the legal notice or not is merely a disputed question of fact and the same should be decided at the trial and the plea of the petitioner is nothing but a defence plea and on the basis of such defence plea the criminal proceeding should not be stifled before the trial specially when there is a prima facie case for going for trial and further the trial of the case has already been concluded and the case is pending for argument no at this stage the application for quashing is not entertainable as in the case of Golam Sarwar Haru vs. The State and another reported in 13 MLR (AD) 103 it has been held that quashment of proceedings, at the stage when trial already began and prosecution witnesses are being examined, is not permissible.
